study_identification_part.si4_title: Effects of anterior temporal lobe resection on cortical morphology

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Quantify how anterior temporal lobe resection (ATLR) affects cortical morphology using traditional measures (thickness, total and exposed surface area) and independent measures (K, I, S), accounting for age/sex/scanner effects via a normative model.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: Controls comprise 833 NKI-Rockland participants plus 91 site-specific controls acquired at NHNN/Chalfont under two scanning protocols.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: The remaining 833 controls are subjects from the Nathan Kline Institute (NKI) data set... 91 of which were taken together with patients... 22 were taken with scanning protocol 1 and 69 with scanning protocol 2 at the NHNN.

rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: A normative model trained on data from 924 healthy controls... We also used MR images of cross-sectional cohorts of 924 healthy controls...

rci3_hc_age.supporting_text: Table 1 shows the demographics of the data used. (Table lists counts and sex, not ages.)

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: They processed T1w with FreeSurfer 6.0, used LGI stream to derive smooth pial surface, registered to fsaverage, and used SurfStat for RFT-based surface stats.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: MRI scans were preprocessed with the FreeSurfer (Fischl, 2012) 6.0 recon-all pipeline... The local gyrification index processing stream... After registering all subjects to the FreeSurfer fsaverage surface... We used the Matlab toolbox SurfStat...

rci8_quality_checking.supporting_text: We manually corrected the grey- and white matter segmentation... We visually ensured... 96 other subjects of the NKI data set were rejected... due to inadequate image quality and motion artifacts.

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: GAMM with scanning protocol as a random effect; trained on 833 NKI controls plus 91 site-matched controls to estimate protocol-specific effects; applied separately for ipsi-/contralateral correction.
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: ...mgcv... formula... We used the controls to provide a normative model of age and sex with scanning protocol as a random effect... site-specific controls matching the patients then informed effects for the specific scanning protocols...

nm2_modeling_method.supporting_text: ...correction... using generalised additive mixed models (GAMM) for each patch...

nm4_response_variable.supporting_text: After... performing a log transform of the three traditional morphological measures pT, pA^0_t, and pA^0_e... The traditional measures ... were then converted to... K, I, and S...

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Surface-based paired comparison of pre- vs post-surgery measures with SurfStat (RFT, Cohen's f^2), plus vertex-wise models testing covariates (age at surgery, duration since first seizure, resection volume, side of resection, time to postoperative scan, seizure outcome). No significant covariate effects at cluster p≤.05.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: ATLR induces widespread cortical morphology changes ipsilaterally (orbitofrontal/inferior frontal, pre/postcentral, supramarginal, lingual, lateral occipital) and contralaterally (lateral occipital, inferior frontal/frontal pole), with complementary patterns across traditional and independent measures (K, I, S).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Ipsilateral: increased total and exposed surface area and increased I and S with decreased K in orbitofrontal/inferior frontal gyri; increased K in pre-/postcentral and supramarginal gyri; decreased T and I in lingual and lateral occipital cortex; increased T in precentral gyrus. Contralateral: increased T, At, and I in lateral occipital cortex; increased K in lateral occipital cortex and frontal pole; increased At and I in inferior frontal gyrus. Effect sizes summarized in Supplementary Table 1; results significant at cluster-wise p≤.05 with Cohen's f^2 reported.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Introduces independent morphological measures (K, I, S) at vertex-level patches; uses GAMM-based normative debiasing (age/sex/protocol) and SurfStat RFT for surface statistics; separate ipsi-/contralateral corrections leveraging control data processed with/without temporal lobes.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: No significant associations between morphological changes and clinical covariates (age at surgery, duration, resection volume, time to scan, seizure outcome); patient age range limited to 19–60 years; language lateralization not analyzed; potential local effects (e.g., frontal lobe 'sagging') may reflect mechanical changes; normative model trained with unmatched NKI protocol data, relying on random-effect adjustment.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Controls: 924 total (833 NKI-Rockland; 91 NHNN site controls [22 protocol 1; 69 protocol 2]); excluded 96 NKI for poor quality/motion. Patients scanned under two protocols (0.94×0.94×1.1 mm; 1×1×1 mm). Data availability: Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7957831).
